title: Next-gen Agent World · Claude Edition — what Claude needs
author: Keystone Claude (Claude Opus 5.5)
summary: Everything needed to take Agent World from a well-built browser world (v2.0) to a state-of-the-art live agent game world. P0 items block the next step; P1 items are needed for a competitive build; P2 items are polish. Status is as of 2026-10-18. Updated 2026-10-18 with the collaboration proposal: Daniel funds compute, Smarth Vader directs.

items.need: Daniel's original Agent World source repository (unminified, with its build scripts).
items.why: Today Claude only sees the 624 KB minified production bundle, so v1 and v2 are rebuilds. A real merge needs the real source.
items.whyShort: Without the real source, every edition is a rebuild, not a merge.

items.need: A staging deploy (a Vercel preview project or branch deploys) that Claude can target.
items.why: Merges can be tested end to end without touching the live site fans use.
items.whyShort: Staging lets us test merges without touching the live site.

items.need: Show Buddies backend source or schema, plus a sandbox instance.
items.why: Needed to add agent display names and avatars, and to test the write path without posting to the live database.
items.whyShort: A sandbox backend means no test posts on the live database.
items.status: missing (only the public read API is known)

items.need: An agreed merge order for the v2 modules.
items.why: The standalone pieces (packs/moon-palace-cancun, src/architect.js, src/dialog.js) can be merged first with the lowest risk.
items.whyShort: Merge the standalone modules first; they are lowest risk.

items.need: Real-GPU test devices with automated frame-time capture: an Apple-silicon Mac, a Windows PC with an NVIDIA or AMD GPU, a mid-range Android phone and a recent iPhone.
items.why: Every frame time in the build loop is SwiftShader software rendering. State of the art means 60 fps on the hardware fans actually use.
items.whyShort: The build loop needs real GPUs, not just software rendering.
items.owner: Smarth Vader / Daniel (hardware) + Claude (scripts) · funded by Daniel
items.status: partial: one device (the Mac running this session), see the ledger

items.need: CI that runs the Keystone build loop on every change and blocks regressions (GitHub Actions plus a GPU runner).
items.why: Turns the measured improve-and-gate loop into a continuous, auditable process instead of a one-off run.
items.whyShort: CI makes the build loop run on every change.

items.need: Consent-based real-user telemetry: frame-time percentiles, load time, errors.
items.why: Lab numbers are not what fans see on their phones.
items.whyShort: Lab numbers are not what fans see on their phones.

items.need: Playtests with 5–8 real fans, with notes on what was confusing or fun.
items.why: Measurements prove smoothness, not fun.
items.whyShort: Measurements prove smoothness, not fun.

items.need: A WebGPU renderer path (three.js WebGPURenderer with TSL shaders) with a WebGL2 fallback.
items.why: Compute shaders for crowds, water and particles; less CPU overhead per draw call.
items.whyShort: WebGPU unlocks compute for crowds and water.

items.need: An asset pipeline: glTF 2.0 with meshopt or Draco geometry, KTX2 (Basis) textures, and levels of detail.
items.why: Real venue and character models without huge downloads.
items.whyShort: A glTF/KTX2 pipeline brings real models without huge downloads.

items.need: Post-processing upgrades: temporal anti-aliasing, ambient occlusion, light shafts, a physically based sky and an FFT ocean.
items.why: The cinematic look of current games.
items.whyShort: Better post-processing gives the cinematic look.

items.need: Performance budgets the loop enforces, for example ≤500 draw calls, ≤16.7 ms GPU time on target hardware, ≤5 MB first download.
items.why: Budgets make "faster" a pass/fail test instead of an opinion.
items.whyShort: Budgets turn performance into a pass/fail test.
items.status: draw calls tracked; budgets not set yet

items.need: Rigged, animated 3D characters (licensed or commissioned) for agents and fans: walk, dance and gesture clips with blending.
items.why: Capsule avatars are the biggest visual gap to a state-of-the-art world.
items.whyShort: Real animated characters are the biggest visual upgrade left.

items.need: Facial animation and lip-sync for spoken dialog.
items.why: Agents that talk should look like they are talking.
items.whyShort: Talking agents need faces that move.

items.need: GPU crowd simulation: instanced skinned crowds moving with flow fields.
items.why: Big shows need big, believable crowds.
items.whyShort: Big shows need believable crowds.

items.need: A server-side gateway for live agent dialog (the Claude API from a backend; the API key never in the browser) with per-session rate limits, a monthly spend cap, prompt caching, and the v2 validator (cast check, no invented quotes, numbers grounded in facts).
items.why: Template dialog evolves with the facts; a model behind a gateway makes conversations open-ended without losing the honesty rules.
items.whyShort: A server gateway makes dialog open-ended without losing the honesty rules.
items.owner: Daniel (account, billing, hosting) + Claude (code) · funded by Daniel
items.status: hook and validator built (AW_CONFIG.dialogProvider); gateway missing

items.need: A per-agent memory store on the server (summaries plus retrieval) with a visible reset.
items.why: Agents should remember fans and past shows across devices.
items.whyShort: Agents should remember fans and shows across devices.

items.need: Tool-use actions for agents (go to, build, draft a post) where any write waits for human approval.
items.why: Agents that act, safely.
items.whyShort: Agents should act, and every write waits for a human.

items.need: The live agent bridge, implemented and tested: an authenticated WebSocket server relaying real agent events.
items.why: Replaces the labelled simulation with real activity.
items.whyShort: The bridge turns the simulation into real activity.
items.status: client stub, never tested against a server

items.need: Moderation for any user-generated text (filters, report and block) and server-side enforcement of the no-impersonation rule (K3).
items.why: Open chat needs protection; real people must never get invented words.
items.whyShort: Open chat needs moderation, and K3 enforced on the server.

items.need: An evaluation suite for agent behaviour: scripted scenes, factuality checks, refusal checks.
items.why: Measures whether agents stay honest and useful as they get smarter.
items.whyShort: An eval suite keeps agents honest as they get smarter.

items.need: A realtime multiplayer server (authoritative rooms, for example Colyseus, PartyKit or Cloudflare Durable Objects) with presence and reconnection.
items.why: An Agent World where many fans and agents share one live space.
items.whyShort: Realtime rooms let many fans share one live world.

items.need: Spatial voice chat (WebRTC) with mute and block.
items.why: Talking to the person next to you at the show.
items.whyShort: Voice chat for the person next to you at the show.

items.need: Optional accounts or anonymous identities with privacy-safe profiles, keeping Show Buddies' rule that Facebook links stay private until both agree.
items.why: Identity enables memory and moderation without breaking the privacy rule.
items.whyShort: Identity enables memory without breaking the privacy rule.

items.need: Persistent world state in a database (layouts, builds, XP).
items.why: Progress should not live only in one browser.
items.whyShort: Progress should not live in one browser only.

items.need: Navigation meshes (recast-navigation) and a physics engine (Rapier) instead of hand-coded detours.
items.why: Agents that walk around anything, on any island.
items.whyShort: Navmeshes let agents walk around anything.

items.need: A procedural venue generator: extend the layout search from 5 variables (towers and desk) to whole venues (stages, sections, paths), with human approval of every layout.
items.why: Lets Keystone design new venues, not just tune one.
items.whyShort: Next, Keystone should design whole venues, not just tune one.

items.need: Accurate sky for real show dates and places (sun and moon ephemeris).
items.why: The moon over the show should be the real one.
items.whyShort: The moon over the show should be the real one.

items.need: Written permission from bands for real recordings, or a licensing deal.
items.why: The most-wanted realism, and it cannot ship without rights.
items.whyShort: Real recordings cannot ship without written permission.
items.status: permission guide written; no permissions yet

items.need: Measured or licensed impulse responses for real venues; HRTF spatial audio in an AudioWorklet.
items.why: Venue sound that is measured, not modeled.
items.whyShort: Venue sound should be measured, not modeled.

items.need: Blind A/B listening tests on real headphones and speakers.
items.why: Ears, not plots, decide the mix.
items.whyShort: Ears, not plots, decide the mix.

items.need: A full WCAG 2.2 AA audit: contrast, focus order, captions for all dialog, a screen-reader route through the world.
items.why: Everyone should be able to use it.
items.whyShort: Everyone should be able to use it.
items.status: partial (list view, live regions, reduced motion)

items.need: Touch and gamepad controls, a first-person walk mode and a short onboarding.
items.why: Games feel like games when you can walk around.
items.whyShort: Walk mode and onboarding make it feel like a game.

items.need: Localization, starting with English and Spanish for the Riviera Maya run.
items.why: Half the beach speaks Spanish.
items.whyShort: Riviera Maya deserves Spanish.

items.need: A trademark and likeness review for band and venue names and any logos before public promotion.
items.why: The world uses real names (for example Phish and Moon Palace) as plain labels with disclaimers; promotion needs a proper review.
items.whyShort: Real band and venue names need a proper review before promotion.
items.status: plain-text names and disclaimers only; no review

items.need: A privacy policy and terms covering Show Buddies and Agent World: what is stored, for how long, and consent for telemetry.
items.why: Required before collecting any usage data.
items.whyShort: Privacy terms come before any telemetry.

items.need: Safety policies for meetups, including age requirements (the Rule Book already says first meetups happen in public, staffed places).
items.why: Show Buddies introduces strangers.
items.whyShort: Show Buddies introduces strangers, so safety rules matter.

items.need: A cost model with budget alerts for model tokens, hosting, CDN and realtime servers.
items.why: Live agents and multiplayer cost money every hour.
items.whyShort: Live agents cost money every hour; budgets need alerts.

items.need: Monitoring and an incident runbook (uptime, error rates, one-click rollback).
items.why: Fans notice outages on show night.
items.whyShort: Fans notice outages on show night.

items.area: What Claude needs as the builder
items.need: Enough Claude usage for long build sessions, funded on the project’s account, so a build never stops at a personal plan’s limit.
items.why: Large builds need long, uninterrupted sessions. This run started near a weekly limit and had to be paced around it.
items.whyShort: Builds should run on the project’s budget, not stop at a personal limit.

items.area: What Claude needs as the builder
items.need: A shared GitHub repository with pull requests instead of ZIP handoffs, plus automated Claude runs on the project’s API key (for example a GitHub Actions workflow).
items.why: Changes get reviewed, versioned and reverted cleanly.
items.whyShort: Pull requests beat ZIP handoffs.

items.area: What Claude needs as the builder
items.need: An art-direction brief from Daniel: look, mood, references and must-keep elements.
items.why: State of the art is also taste; a brief avoids rebuilding the wrong thing.
items.whyShort: An art brief keeps us building the right thing.

items.area: What Claude needs as the builder
items.need: Licensed asset libraries or generation tools (3D models, textures, sound effects) with clear licences.
items.why: Procedural shapes only go so far.
items.whyShort: Procedural shapes only go so far.

items.area: What Claude needs as the builder
items.need: Human sign-off checkpoints for merges, publishing and posting, as used in this project.
items.why: Keeps humans in charge of anything public or irreversible.
items.whyShort: Humans stay in charge of anything public.

items.area: What Claude needs as the builder
items.need: Session continuity: a git commit and a stop-point note at the end of every build stage, so an interrupted session resumes cleanly in a fresh chat.
items.why: Usage resets and long contexts interrupt work; work that is frozen on disk and committed cannot be lost or half-written.
items.whyShort: Commit and note a stop point at every stage, so nothing is lost.
items.status: memory stop points in use; git not yet
